lines.text: Do you know how one photo reaches forty strangers, with no names and no numbers?
Sunset on a tiny island. Lena lifts her phone and snaps the whole beach party.
Now everyone shouts the same thing. Send it to me!
But nobody has anyone's number. And a group chat with forty strangers? No thanks.
So she opens Orbi Transfer, sets the code wave, and taps send.
Seconds later, phones light up all along the sand.
Hold on. Let's freeze time and look inside.
First, the photo is locked right on her phone. The code becomes the key, and the key never leaves her hand.
Then it splits into pieces, and they fly up together, side by side. That's why it's quick.
The pieces wait in a vault, still scrambled. Even the vault can't read them.
Now Orbi rings the screens in this rough area, about forty by twenty kilometres. Never her exact spot.
Sam taps the photo and types wave. The pieces drop, click together, and unlock on his phone.
Thirty minutes later, the vault burns every piece. No account. No trace.
Only want your friends? Make a private Space with a passcode. Strangers never even see it.
orbitransfer.com. Try it on two phones!
